clue.text: Wrong to send volunteers round on service call

indicators.note: to send something round is to turn it about so it faces the other way

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
in tennis the umpire calls 'fault' on a bad serve

explanation.surface: Someone criticises the dispatch of volunteers on a call-out to service something.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve. 'Service' is a tennis serve, and FAULT is the umpire's call when it misses.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at fault is to be in the wrong, blameworthy for an error.

clue.text: Briefly try tool starting engine on riverboat

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, then shortened
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes
the first letter of engine
the river half of this word gives R, the standard abbreviation for river; the boat half is the definition

explanation.surface: Someone tests a tool to get the engine going on a boat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riverboat' reads as one word, but it splits: 'river' gives R and 'boat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trawler is a fishing vessel that drags a net, so it is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Notice a point to change

blocks.note: an advertisement, a notice put up or printed
taken as written
PT is the usual abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: Someone spots a detail in a document that needs altering.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to modify or adjust, so it is a synonym for change as a verb.

clue.text: Hide note in flap

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, enclosed on both sides

blocks.note: to be in a lather, or a flap, is to be agitated
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A musical note is tucked away inside a fold of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal skin, and hide is the word for a raw animal skin.

clue.text: Sympathy and strong wine offered after knock

indicators.note: something offered after another comes later in sequence, so it follows on

blocks.note: a rap is a sharp knock
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A visitor knocks at the door and is consoled with a glass of strong wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, understanding relationship, so it conveys mutual sympathy between people.

clue.text: Sum total for a horse?

blocks.note: taken as written
a mount is a horse that is ridden

explanation.surface: A question about how much money a horse will cost.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity or total, the figure that a sum comes to.

clue.text: I merit VIP treatment! Simple!

indicators.note: treatment means handling or working on something, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-important person demands special treatment, and a bystander scoffs at how naive that is.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means basic or crude, undeveloped, which is the same as simple in style.

clue.text: Once more supply soldier with ecstasy and crack

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: A soldier is handed drugs, ecstasy and crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' sounds like the drug next to ecstasy, but it means a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-equip is to provide fresh gear or equipment again, so it means to supply once more.

clue.text: Hard stuff with tonic, say, for the builder's assistant?

blocks.note: concrete is a hard building material
tonic water is an example of a drink mixed with spirits

explanation.surface: Hard liquor with a splash of tonic for a builder's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' reads as strong spirits, which pairs naturally with tonic, but it is the building material.
explanation.definitionFit: A cement mixer is a machine that helps a builder prepare the material, a mechanical helper on site.

clue.text: Lady singer with good range

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
an Aga is a British brand of kitchen range cooker

explanation.surface: A woman singer with an impressive vocal range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests vocal range, but it is a cooking stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Gaga is the stage name of a pop star, so the surname completes the phrase 'Lady singer'.

clue.text: Said sorry for serving old sago pie

indicators.note: food being served is dished up and spread about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook makes amends for dishing up a stale pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to express regret, which is what saying sorry does.

clue.text: Firm grasp needed to operate the gears

blocks.note: first meaning: a tight grip
second meaning: the pedal in a car used when changing gear

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as advice on driving; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a tight grip on something and the pedal mechanism a driver uses to engage gears.

clue.text: Keep on against money, upper class and, ultimately, privilege

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: as in pros and cons
tin is old slang for money
U is the label for upper-class usage
the last letter of privilege

explanation.surface: A protest against wealth, the upper class and, finally, privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from a 1950s British essay sorting words into U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue is to carry on or persist, which is what keeping on means.

clue.text: Corgi runs round Queen's legs regularly for food

indicators.note: a dog that runs about scrambles here and there, so these letters move into a new order
to go round something is to surround it on both sides
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher
the second and fourth letters of legs

explanation.surface: A royal corgi scampers around the Queen's legs, as it often does, hoping for a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The late Queen Elizabeth II famously kept corgis, which makes the picture natural; 'legs' is only a source of letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Groceries are household food and supplies bought from a shop, so food is a fair general term.

clue.text: Jug meant for coffee surprisingly produces fierce tea!

indicators.note: a surprising result is an unexpected one, so these letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A coffee pot unexpectedly brews a powerful cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafetiere is a glass pot with a plunger, the French press used for brewing coffee.

clue.text: Biting cold?

blocks.note: first meaning: inclined to nip, as a snappy dog
second meaning: chilly, as of the weather

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase for a sharp chill, but 'Biting' is its own meaning: given to nipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy describes a dog that nips and also weather that is sharply chilly.

clue.text: Handle's extremely smooth at the back

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of smooth
aft is the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: A tool's handle is described as very smooth at its rear end.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaft of a tool such as a golf club or axe is its long handle.

clue.text: They try to have us on trip ashore round about 10

definitions.text: They try to have us on

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so these letters fall out of order
going round about something encircles it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Tricksters who fool people on a trip ashore at around ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like an outing, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoaxers play deceptive tricks, and to have someone on is to fool or tease them.

clue.text: Call to admire trick poetry she composed

indicators.note: composed means put together or written, so these letters are assembled afresh

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer asks people to admire a clever trick in the verse she wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey presto is the magician's exclamation inviting the audience to marvel at a completed illusion.

clue.text: Pupil ate spinach as part of an exercise programme

indicators.note: part of means only a piece, so the letters sit within the words before

blocks.note: read across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A schoolchild eats greens as part of a healthy fitness regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a system of exercises focusing on core strength, flexibility and posture.

clue.text: Diplomatic about fault hampering medical scanner

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so these letters are turned into a new order
something hampering another hems it in, here closing around it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a CT scanner takes computed tomography images

explanation.surface: A tactful word about a breakdown that is holding up a hospital scanner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tactful means handling people with sensitivity, which is what a diplomatic person does.

clue.text: Didn't take part when turned back by solicitor

indicators.note: turned back means facing the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: as in 'as I left', meaning when
a tout solicits custom, selling tickets or touting for business

explanation.surface: Someone stays out of the case after being sent away by a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but it is anyone who solicits business: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit out a dance or game is to stay on the sidelines rather than join in.

clue.text: Meat that's processed is apt to absorb stuff

indicators.note: processing changes a material's form, so these letters are reworked
to absorb something is to take it inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Processed meat is said to soak up fillers and additives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun but is the verb, to cram.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured, spiced and smoked beef, a deli meat that is indeed processed.

clue.text: Support a heartless crony to get bequest

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is removed, leaving only the ends

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or chair
taken as written
the first and last letters of crony

explanation.surface: Someone backs an unfeeling friend so as to land an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is money or property left in a will, which is what a bequest is.

clue.text: Good morning, Mum! There's a letter from Greece

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the morning
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A child greets their mother at breakfast and hands over post from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' reads as post, but it is a character of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Good to live with new love at sea, getting space and time

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so these letters are muddled

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
N is the abbreviation for new
the letters to be rearranged
an en is a printer's space
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A romantic plan to live with a new partner on a cruise, with room and time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing measure, a space half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolent means kindly and well-meaning, so it is a synonym for good in character.

clue.text: Miss a hand-warmer!

blocks.note: first meaning: to bungle, as dropping a catch
second meaning: a fur tube for keeping hands warm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman owning a hand-warmer, but it is a verb meaning to fumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To muff a chance is to bungle it, and a muff is a tube of fur worn to warm the hands.

clue.text: Looks at specs for building

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are assembled in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone examines the specifications for a construction project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks at' runs together as a phrase, but 'Looks' alone is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is an appearance or look, as in a building's grim aspect.

clue.text: American university gets everyone young, as a rule

blocks.note: US is the abbreviation for American
U is the abbreviation for university
all means everyone
Y is the abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: An American college typically admits all its students young.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually means normally or in most cases, which is what 'as a rule' expresses.
